concept.name: Template-switching reverse transcription
concept.substrate: Primed RNA in an RNA-containing reaction, together with a reverse transcriptase, nucleotides and a template-switching oligonucleotide.
concept.operation: Synthesize first-strand cDNA from RNA and perform template switching to introduce an oligonucleotide-derived terminal sequence into the cDNA synthesis product.
concept.physical_mechanism: Reverse-transcriptase-mediated copying of RNA coupled to use of a template-switching oligonucleotide as a further synthesis template. This describes the enzyme/template transition; an exact terminal nucleotide structure or complete strand-level reaction is not required or inferred.
concept.output: A first-strand cDNA/template-switch reaction carrying RNA-derived sequence and a template-switch-derived handle suitable for the stated downstream amplification route.
concept.information_effect: Transfers RNA sequence into cDNA and adds a synthetic amplification handle associated with RNA-end capture. Full-length recovery of every RNA, strand retention and original-molecule identity are separate properties requiring evidence.
concept.purpose: Make RNA-derived cDNA accessible to subsequent amplification through template switching.
concept.context_requirements: Membership requires RNA-to-cDNA synthesis coupled to template switching within the represented transformation. Priming strategy, RNA-input scale, oligonucleotide modifications, incubation conditions and purification choices remain contextual properties.

case.question: Which RNA-to-cDNA transformations install an amplification handle by template switching, and how do they differ from installing adaptors on pre-existing DNA?
case.existing_plus_filters: The frozen catalogue has concepts={} and the actual lookup 'input transformation output' returned no candidates; there is no existing definition to reuse. The filter alternative was examined with selections find 'template' in operations (Smart-seq2), 'transpos*' in operations (the DNA transposition/repair cut), and 'barcode' in operations (RAD-seq and DBiT-seq). These fields can retrieve this observed implementation, but a generic handle-installation label does not define the RNA-copying/template-switch transition. Admit one mechanism-level anchor; RNA input scale, TSO chemistry and cleanup choices remain filters rather than additional labels.
case.lost_distinction_if_merged: Merging with generic adaptor/handle installation would conceal whether RNA is copied into a new DNA molecule or existing DNA is fragmented or ligated. Those input/output and enzyme dependencies matter to comparing protocol transformations. No additional category is justified for the observed LNA base, single-cell scale or omitted bead cleanup.
properties_to_preserve: Required membership is RNA copying coupled to template switching. The selected occurrence comprises reverse_transcribe, including the reported RT inactivation, and ends at the unpurified first_strand reaction; amplification and subsequent tagmentation are downstream.

Observed input alternatives are an individually handled single-cell lysate or a separately handled total-RNA sample, not a physical mixture of these alternatives. The upstream priming uses anchored oligo-dT 5′-AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTACT30VN-3′ and dNTPs after 72 °C for 3 min and immediate cooling.

Reported 7 µl first-strand mix: 0.50 µl SuperScript II RT, 200 U/µl (Invitrogen); 0.25 µl RNase inhibitor, 40 U/µl (Clontech); 2 µl 5× SuperScript II First-Strand Buffer (Invitrogen); 0.25 µl 100 mM DTT (Invitrogen); 2 µl 5 M betaine (Sigma); 0.9 µl 100 mM MgCl2 (Sigma); 1 µl 10 µM TSO; 0.1 µl nuclease-free water (Gibco). These are stock/addition amounts, not reconciled single-cell final concentrations.

Observed selected TSO: 1 µl at 10 µM, 5′-AAGCAGTGGTATCAACGCAGAGTACrGrG+G-3′; two riboguanosines and terminal LNA guanosine. Table 2 is a tested inventory; Table 4 selects rGrG+G. LNA chemistry is not a condition of category membership.
42 °C 90 min; ten cycles 50 °C 2 min / 42 °C 2 min; 70 °C 15 min RT inactivation.

Observed output routing: no bead purification between first-strand synthesis and preamplification in the selected variant. KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix is the downstream preamplification choice, not an additional enzyme silently inserted into this cut.

Information interpretation: common oligo-dT/TSO/ISPCR amplification-handle sequence is inferred from sequences and downstream use. RNA 5′-end capture is an associated purpose; complete transcript recovery, strand identity and an original-molecule barcode are not established.
Unresolved: exact terminal nucleotide/covalent structure and the detailed template-switch transition are not strand-resolved in the inspected passages.

Unresolved single-cell final volume: 2 µl lysis buffer plus 1 µl oligo-dT, 1 µl dNTPs and the printed 7 µl RT addition totals 11 µl before carryover, whereas another Methods statement uses 10 µl first-strand volume. The total-RNA alternative begins with 1 µl RNA. Preserve addition/stock amounts, without inventing a common correction or single-cell final concentrations.

decisions.review_rationale: Admit. The useful question is which RNA-copying transformations install an amplification handle by template switching, as opposed to modifying pre-existing DNA. The single frozen-registry lookup returned no candidates; there is no existing concept-plus-filters solution. Independently repeated selection searches found 'template' only in Smart-seq2 and 'transpos*' only in the DNA fragmentation/repair cut. A raw template word can retrieve this occurrence but does not define the coupled RNA-to-cDNA/template-transition interface. Merging into generic handle attachment would obscure substrate copying and template-switch dependence, so a mechanism-level singleton is justified without demanding repeated examples. Required membership is coupled RNA copying and template switching; single-cell versus total-RNA input, anchored priming, TSO LNA chemistry, concentrations, temperatures and omitted cleanup remain use properties. The definition provides input, action, output, information role and context, while preserving uncertainty about strand-level end structure and recovery. The two supplied negative boundaries are supported at their selected cuts. No experimental substitution, ancestry or complete-recipe claim follows.
source_review_rationales: The sole assigned occurrence satisfies RNA-to-cDNA synthesis coupled to template switching: primed total-RNA or single-cell-lysate inputs enter SuperScript II/TSO synthesis, followed by the reported RT inactivation, and the selected rGrG+G variant proceeds without bead cleanup to downstream amplification. The common amplification handle is a sequence-based inference, not a resolved terminal-structure measurement. Upstream priming and downstream preamplification/tagmentation are not added to this cut. The quoted methods are interleaved PDF columns and are interpreted with the table headers and neighboring methods, without treating unrelated sequencing/PCR text as RT ingredients.

boundary_examples.reason: The selected RNA-primed reaction uses reverse transcription and the selected rGrG+G TSO, yielding first-strand material for direct amplification.
This cut supplies sequencing-access sequences by transposase fragmentation of prepared genomic DNA and then nick translation; it does not copy RNA with a TSO.

The supplied DBiT selection is the second-flow A/B ligation step. Its earlier reverse transcription and later template switching are outside this occurrence; their presence elsewhere in the paper does not make this cut a member.

concept.name: Transposase adaptor insertion followed by polymerase repair
concept.substrate: Prepared double-stranded DNA and transposase complexes loaded with synthetic sequencing-adaptor oligonucleotides.
concept.operation: Fragment DNA while transferring adaptor sequences to the fragments by transposition, then process the resulting adaptor-bearing intermediate with DNA polymerase to reach the stated repaired-library boundary.
concept.physical_mechanism: Transposase-catalyzed fragmentation and adaptor end joining, followed by polymerase-mediated end processing reported here as nick translation. Exact offset, short-strand fate, transposase release and residual covalent discontinuities are not specified by this mechanism-level category.
concept.output: Adaptor-bearing DNA fragment library after the represented polymerase repair step; the actual use must state what sequencing compatibility is reported and what strand structure remains unknown.
concept.information_effect: Preserves genomic insert sequence within newly delimited fragments and installs sequencing-access domains. Fragment boundaries and any insertion/representation bias are contextual; this operation does not itself record a pre-existing pairwise interaction or establish a provenance barcode.
concept.purpose: Convert DNA into adaptor-bearing fragments with the polymerase processing needed for the reported library endpoint.
concept.context_requirements: Membership requires both coupled transposase fragmentation/adaptor transfer and polymerase processing of that intermediate. Prepared transposomes are an input; their assembly and downstream cleanup/readout are separate boundaries. Adaptor brand, species, sample mass, temperature and whether a larger workflow later uses PCR do not define membership.

case.question: Which transformations convert DNA through transposase-mediated fragmentation/adaptor transfer and a subsequent polymerase-processing step to the reported repaired-library endpoint?
case.existing_plus_filters: The frozen catalogue is empty; the actual lookup 'input transformation output' yielded no definition to reuse. selections find 'transpos*' in operations retrieves this two-operation cut, while 'ligation' retrieves RAD-seq, DBiT-seq, Hi-C and hiCLIP. A hypothetical well-defined transposition concept with a repair property could support this query, but none exists in the frozen catalogue. The admitted definition states the whole two-stage transition rather than leaving the repaired output implicit in a bare tagmentation term. Species, NoPCR adaptor design, FailSafe identity, PCR-free production status, amounts and conditions remain use properties. No separate category is created for each such combination.
case.lost_distinction_if_merged: A category that stops at fragmentation/adaptor insertion would collapse the tagmented intermediate into the reported post-nick-translation library, losing the polymerase dependency and the uncertainty about final strand continuity. A generic ligation label would also miss the coupled creation of fragment boundaries by transposase. The two-stage boundary is scientifically useful despite being a singleton; repetition is not the admission rationale.
properties_to_preserve: Required membership is the connected two-stage transition: tagment(genomic_dna + prepared_transposomes) -> tagmented_dna -> nick_translate -> unpurified nick_translated_library. Array order in the extraction is not chemical order. Both actual operations remain explicit.

Observed genomic inputs: previously prepared bacterial or human genomic DNA, 100 or 200 ng. DNA isolation and transposome assembly are upstream; the defined output stops before the reported subsequent MinElute cleanup.

Observed transposome input: Ez-Tn5 complexes assembled with NoPCR1/NoPCR2 and a phosphorylated 19-base ME reverse complement. NoPCR adaptors supply P1/P2 cluster-compatibility domains at transposition rather than introducing them during production PCR. Full reported NoPCR sequences remain on the bound occurrence.
100 or 200 ng prepared genomic DNA and 5 μl prepared custom transposomes.
2 μl 5× Nextera HMW buffer (Epicentre), with water to 10 μl reaction volume.
55°C for 5 min.
Observed repair resource: 25 μl 2× FailSafe PCR master mix (Epicentre), 1 μl FailSafe DNA polymerase (Epicentre), and 14 μl nuclease-free water (Ambion), added to the tagmentation reaction.

Observed repair condition: 72 °C for 5 min. FailSafe PCR master mix is a reagent identity; this incubation is reported as nick translation, with no production-library PCR cycling in this selected route.

Information effect: sequence-access domains are installed on fragments whose boundaries are created by transposition. The original PCR-free route is intended to reduce PCR-associated representation bias, not guarantee bias-free recovery or create an interaction record.

Intermediate/output uncertainty: strand offsets or gap length, exact strand replacement, fate of the annealed short ME strand, how transposase releases and any residual nick/covalent discontinuity are unresolved. Preserve the authors' Illumina-ready endpoint without asserting completely sealed duplexes or inventing a ligase or pre-repair removal step.

Representation limits: discussion reports limited insert-size-distribution control and greater high-G+C bias than conventional methods, with possible partial correction through PCR-free handling. These are qualified context observations, not membership conditions or a universal bias model.

PCR-free refers to production preparation; flow-cell cluster amplification and the separately sampled analytical real-time-PCR branch belong to other boundaries. No analytical amplification product is routed into this production cut.

decisions.review_rationale: Admit. The comparison question concerns the completed DNA-to-adaptor-library transition that passes through transposase fragmentation/adaptor transfer and a subsequent polymerase-processing dependency. The empty frozen registry provides no existing definition to filter; the independent 'transpos*' operation search retrieves this cut, while 'ligation' retrieves four different joining cuts. These lexical results alone do not warrant admission. The consequential boundary is independently supported by the source: post-transposition material precedes the reported nick-translation step and is not the stated Illumina-ready endpoint. Requiring both stages therefore preserves a material-interface distinction relevant to comparing downstream library readiness. This composite is justified by that question and dependency, rather than by the selected module or the NoPCR brand. Its two operations must remain explicit. A future general transposition anchor with structured repair/endpoint properties could support overlapping retrieval, but none is available for reuse here, and this review creates no competing replacement. Species, input mass, adaptor design, FailSafe identity, PCR-free production status, cleanup boundary and conditions remain properties. Strand offsets, strand replacement, transposase release and complete sealing remain unknown. Actual negative examples support the mechanism boundary; a singleton is sufficient.
source_review_rationales: The complete assigned cut is supported in chemical order: prepared DNA plus prepared NoPCR transposomes undergo fragmentation/adaptor transfer, then the same reaction receives FailSafe polymerase resources for nick translation, ending before MinElute cleanup. The source calls this an Illumina-ready PCR-free production route. The two selected operations and intermediate must remain explicit; neither the background's limited-cycle PCR nor the separate analytical qPCR branch becomes a production stage. 'Repair' here denotes the reported polymerase processing and compatibility endpoint, not demonstrated full strand sealing, a known gap length or an inferred ligase reaction.

boundary_examples.reason: The same production route explicitly tagmentates genomic DNA and then incubates it with FailSafe DNA polymerase for nick translation to the stated Illumina-ready library.

At the supplied cut, DNA is already restriction-digested; P1 is then attached by T4 DNA-ligase ligation. Later shearing and end processing in the paper do not create this transposase/polymerase sequence.
The selected Smart-seq2 transition is RNA reverse transcription with a TSO. Tagmentation described later in that paper is outside this selected operation.

concept.name: Provenance-barcode installation by ligation
concept.substrate: Analyte-derived DNA or a DNA carrier already linked to analyte sequence, plus a barcode-bearing oligonucleotide assigned to a known sample, spatial region or other handling unit.
concept.operation: Covalently attach the barcode-bearing oligonucleotide to the analyte-linked DNA by ligation while the barcode-to-origin assignment is maintained.
concept.physical_mechanism: DNA-ligase-mediated nucleic-acid end joining. End alignment can use an existing compatible overhang or a complementary splint; those implementations and end chemistries remain distinct properties.
concept.output: Analyte-linked DNA carrying the ligated provenance barcode and any accompanying amplification, affinity or molecule-label domains.
concept.information_effect: Encodes the origin unit handled during labeling as a sequence associated with the analyte, permitting later attribution after pooling or recovery. The code identifies that unit; finer identities and additional UMI interpretation require separate evidence.
concept.purpose: Preserve sample or spatial provenance through subsequent library handling and sequencing.
concept.context_requirements: Membership requires a provenance code carried by the ligated oligonucleotide, a maintained physical barcode-to-origin assignment during joining, and a covalent analyte-linked output. A generic primer site, affinity mark or constant arm-separator alone is insufficient. Sample versus pixel, material support, end geometry, UMI, barcode length and delivery apparatus are contextual properties.

case.question: Which transformations ligate a provenance-bearing barcode onto analyte-linked DNA before subsequent mixing or recovery, and what physical unit can each barcode identify?
case.existing_plus_filters: No existing concepts are present in the frozen catalogue, and the actual lookup 'input transformation output' returned no candidates. selections find 'barcode' in operations returned RAD-seq and DBiT-seq; 'UMI' returned DBiT-seq alone. 'ligation' in operations also retrieves Hi-C and hiCLIP, and the lexical requirements search 'T4 DNA ligase' overlaps with those uses. Thus ligation/enzyme filters alone do not answer the provenance question. Admit a common provenance-barcode-ligation purpose, then filter sample/pool versus pixel, UMI, support and end-alignment geometry. Those property distinctions are sufficient within this shared definition; a separate SbfI/P1/sample-barcode category is unnecessary.
case.lost_distinction_if_merged: Merging provenance installation with all adaptor ligations or all association-recording joins would erase whether a known code is assigned to a handling unit or two endogenous regions are linked as a relationship record. Within the proposed category, sample/pool identity versus spatial identity is consequential but fully retained as a use property; splitting those purposes into separate named concepts is not justified by this cohort.
properties_to_preserve: Required membership is a provenance-bearing oligonucleotide covalently joined to analyte-linked DNA. Observed cut: ligate_p1 consumes the heat-inactivated SbfI digest and outputs P1-ligated restriction fragments. Upstream restriction digestion and downstream pooling/shearing are separate operations.

Observed input is SbfI-digested genomic DNA following 65 °C for 20 min. It can derive from an individual or a pre-existing DNA pool; a single barcode does not resolve constituents mixed before this ligation.

Modified Solexa P1 adapter, SbfI top 5′-AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCTxxxxTGCA-3′; bottom 5′-Phos-xxxxAGATCGGAAGAGCGTCGTGTAGGGAAAGAGTGTAGATCTCGGTGGTCGCCGTATCATT-3′. xxxx is the variable four-base barcode block.
P1 addition: 2.5 µL at 100 nM.
1 µL 100 mM rATP (Promega), 1 µL 10× EcoRI buffer, 0.5 µL high-concentration T4 DNA Ligase (1000 U, NEB), 5 µL water.
Room temperature, 20 min.
Barcode design: all barcodes differ by at least two nucleotides to reduce erroneous sample assignment due to sequencing error.

Observed molecular alignment uses SbfI-compatible overhangs and the printed phosphorylated P1 bottom strand, rather than DBiT's separate universal splint. Full strand sequences are retained above; covalent attachment is the molecular interpretation of reported ligation.
Output carries the P1 forward-amplification site, Illumina sequencing-primer site and sample barcode. This is neither original-molecule labeling nor an encoded two-region proximity measurement.

Barcode length is qualified: the general description says 4 or 5 bases, while the selected SbfI strand pair displays four xxxx positions. Do not import the EcoRI five-position strand pair into this use.

Unresolved: exact SbfI barcode codebook, oligo-to-input assignment, orientation/decoding, mismatch tolerance and ambiguous-code handling. Minimum two-nucleotide separation is reported as an error-reduction design rule, not a recovered error-correction algorithm.
Retain the printed 10× EcoRI buffer addition on this P1 ligation. It does not specify the earlier digestion buffer or license a substitute SbfI reaction recipe.

decisions.review_rationale: Admit the proposed provenance-barcode-ligation definition as a shared-purpose category also used by the DBiT decision. The useful question asks which transformations covalently assign known origin information before later mixing/recovery, and what physical unit the code identifies. No existing definition is available in the frozen registry. Independent property searches found 'barcode' in RAD-seq and DBiT, 'UMI' only in DBiT, and 'ligation' in four selections; the broad lexical T4/DNA/ligase requirements search also returned partial-term matches and is not evidence of a common detailed mechanism. Generic ligation/access-domain installation would lose the barcode-to-origin assignment requirement and conflate provenance with endogenous-region association recording. Within this purpose, the sample/pool versus pixel distinction and overhang versus splint alignment are adequately retained as properties; a separate SbfI/sample-specific category would be unnecessary. Membership requires an assigned code, maintained origin correspondence and covalent analyte-linked output, not a particular barcode length, enzyme brand or support. The other member and both negative boundary claims are supported by their own sources. Shared purpose does not make these experiments interchangeable.
source_review_rationales: The sole assigned P1 operation ligates a barcode-bearing adaptor to the already heat-inactivated SbfI digest using T4 DNA ligase. Its four-position SbfI code and primer domains persist on restriction fragments before subsequent pooling and shearing. Individual and already pooled inputs are both reported, so provenance means the ligation input rather than each constituent of a pre-existing pool. The source supports the entire selected input/action/output and information role, with no UMI or pairwise-interaction claim. Digestion, later inactivation and subsequent library processing remain outside the cut.

boundary_examples.reason: P1 ligation attaches a sample-identifying barcode to a genomic restriction fragment; the code denotes the handled ligation input.
Second-flow ligation joins B to an A-linked analyte carrier, adding the second coordinate of a tissue pixel; this is another provenance unit within the same purpose category.

Although this cut includes adaptor ligation, its A/B are designated cloning/linker adaptors. B joins two RNA arms and marks their boundary; the supplied cut does not install a code assigned to a sample or spatial handling unit.

The selected ligation creates chimeras between chromatin fragments. Biotin marks a ligation-junction class, rather than encoding a sample or pixel identity. This conclusion concerns this cut, not whether some later library might be indexed.

concept.name: Recording physical association by nucleic-acid ligation
concept.substrate: Nucleic-acid segments whose pre-existing physical association is retained in a chromatin or ribonucleoprotein preparation until joining, together with the required ligation reagents and any bridge adaptors.
concept.operation: Ligate the associated segments into a covalent joint construct, directly or through a linker. A contextual use can include connected adaptor attachment and terminal activation required before the segment-joining step.
concept.physical_mechanism: Enzymatic end joining either directly between DNA fragments or between RNA arms through an adaptor, with different ligases, end structures and preparative steps in the individual uses. The shared relation is the recording purpose; these implementations are not asserted to be one detailed mechanism.
concept.output: A product population containing covalent constructs that link two associated nucleic-acid regions for joint sequence readout; unjoined and other byproducts, and separately handled controls, remain properties of the actual use.
concept.information_effect: Converts a retained physical association into a sequence-readable linkage between regions. It does not by itself establish exact distance, base pairing, direct contact, universal true-positive status or a quantitative interaction probability.
concept.purpose: Record relationships between nucleic-acid regions for later paired-region interpretation.
concept.context_requirements: Membership requires that joining two analyte regions is used to record their prior physical association. Merely attaching a known barcode to each analyte in a shared region is insufficient. DNA versus RNA, fixation/capture, direct versus linker-mediated joining, ligases, dilution, support, bridge sequence, controls and downstream biological interpretation remain contextual.

case.question: Which transformations convert retained physical association of two nucleic-acid regions into a covalent sequence-readable linkage, and how do DNA-contact and RNA-duplex implementations differ?
case.existing_plus_filters: The frozen catalogue contains no existing concepts; the actual lookup 'input transformation output' returned no candidates. selections find 'ligation' in operations returned Hi-C, hiCLIP, RAD-seq and DBiT-seq. The information-effect filters 'proximity' and 'duplex' separately retrieved Hi-C and hiCLIP; sources show that both record relationships by joining analyte regions, whereas the other ligations assign known provenance codes. Admit one shared-purpose definition to retrieve the association-recording transition across that terminology, retaining DNA/RNA, fixation/capture, dilution, support and direct/linker-mediated joining as filters. Those filters adequately distinguish the two admitted uses; separate Hi-C-chemistry and hiCLIP-bridge categories are not needed for this comparison question.
case.lost_distinction_if_merged: Merging with generic nucleic-acid ligation would hide the measured relationship: joining two analyte regions that were physically associated differs from adding a known label to a single carrier. DNA contacts and STAU1-associated RNA duplexes are not equivalent observables, but their differences survive in substrate, association context, junction geometry, controls and interpretation properties under a shared-purpose relation.
properties_to_preserve: Required membership is association-recording joining of two analyte regions. Observed cut: ligate_hi_c consumes SDS-inactivated, biotin-filled production chromatin and outputs four separate ligation reactions. The 3C tube is a separate control with a different ligase dose, not another production member.

Physical context: cross-linked, HindIII-digested chromatin has been filled to blunt ends with biotin-14-dCTP before this cut. Retained association and dilute ligation favor joins between previously close regions; this does not prove every join is a direct or biologically meaningful contact.

Each corresponding 15 ml tube contains 7.61 ml mix: 745 μl 10% Triton X-100; 745 μl 10× ligation buffer (500 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 100 mM MgCl2, 100 mM DTT); 80 μl 10 mg/ml BSA; 80 μl 100 mM ATP; 5.96 ml water.
16°C for 4 h.
Per Hi-C tube 2–5: 50 μl 1 U/μl T4 DNA ligase (Invitrogen).

Biotin is inherited from upstream fill-in and retained at joined ends; it is an affinity mark on junctions, not a newly ligated sample barcode. Post-ligation crosslink reversal/purification is downstream.

Observed output: chimeric DNA ligation products, with the expected HindIII AAGCTT-to-NheI GCTAGC junction signature. The reported 70% NheI-only amplicon result is a particular downstream QC observation, not the fraction of all molecules successfully ligated.

Required shared purpose does not equate DNA-chromatin proximity with an RNA duplex, nor dilution with bead-supported capture. Direct T4 DNA-ligase blunt-end joining, absence of an internal B bridge in this cut, substrate state and scale remain comparison properties.

Information limit: a ligation event is a joint sequence record. Exact distance, cell identity, true-positive probability and a calibrated interaction frequency are not specified at this transformation boundary; later enrichment, read mapping and contact normalization are separate.

decisions.review_rationale: Admit the proposed physical-association-recording definition as shared purpose with hiCLIP. The useful retrieval question is which joining transformations convert a retained relationship between two analyte regions into a joint sequence record, and how their observable and chemistry differ. No existing concept is present in the frozen registry. Independently repeated 'ligation' search returns Hi-C, hiCLIP, RAD-seq and DBiT, whereas information-effect filters 'proximity' and 'duplex' retrieve Hi-C and hiCLIP separately. A shared-purpose anchor connects this substantive information transition across terminology and excludes externally assigned provenance ligations; generic end joining would erase that distinction. Hi-C direct blunt-end DNA joining and hiCLIP bridge-mediated RNA joining remain distinct physical implementations, not one detailed mechanism. DNA/RNA substrate, crosslink/capture context, dilution, support, ligases, bridge, controls and downstream interpretation are required use-level comparisons; they do not require separate labels for this purpose. The source-supported inclusion of hiCLIP covers its full attachment/activation/joining path and excludes its omitted-joining control. Both supplied provenance negatives are supported. No exact-distance or universal true-interaction inference is admitted.
source_review_rationales: The sole assigned operation consumes separately retained, filled/SDS-inactivated chromatin and performs dilute T4 DNA-ligase blunt-end joining in four production tubes. The chimeric DNA and biotin-marked junctions are intended to record previous chromatin proximity. Biotin was installed during upstream fill-in; no provenance-code oligonucleotide is joined here. The distinct 3C tube remains a control. HindIII-to-NheI structure is supported for the detailed HindIII implementation and is not generalized to the paper's NcoI alternative. The QC amplicon result does not measure every production molecule or guarantee biological validity of each join.

boundary_examples.reason: Dilute blunt-end ligation of retained cross-linked chromatin creates chimeric DNA for contact readout; pre-existing proximity is the information being recorded.
The production path attaches A/B, activates ends, then joins the two retained RNA-duplex arms through B. This records paired regions; the omission control remains separate.

Spatial proximity of many analytes in a tissue pixel is encoded by assigned A/B labels. The ligation joins barcode segments on an analyte carrier, not two analyte regions whose pairwise molecular association is to be recorded.
P1 joining installs a known sample-identifying barcode on each restriction fragment; it does not preserve a pairwise physical association of two endogenous regions.

case.question: Which transformations ligate a provenance-bearing barcode onto analyte-linked DNA, including a second spatial coordinate, and which code and co-carried domains govern later attribution?
case.existing_plus_filters: The frozen catalogue is empty and the actual lookup 'input transformation output' found no candidate definition. selections find 'barcode' in operations retrieves DBiT-seq and RAD-seq; 'UMI' separates DBiT-seq. concept.name: Recording physical association by nucleic-acid ligation
concept.substrate: Nucleic-acid segments whose pre-existing physical association is retained in a chromatin or ribonucleoprotein preparation until joining, together with the required ligation reagents and any bridge adaptors.
concept.operation: Ligate the associated segments into a covalent joint construct, directly or through a linker. A contextual use can include connected adaptor attachment and terminal activation required before the segment-joining step.
concept.physical_mechanism: Enzymatic end joining either directly between DNA fragments or between RNA arms through an adaptor, with different ligases, end structures and preparative steps in the individual uses. The shared relation is the recording purpose; these implementations are not asserted to be one detailed mechanism.
concept.output: A product population containing covalent constructs that link two associated nucleic-acid regions for joint sequence readout; unjoined and other byproducts, and separately handled controls, remain properties of the actual use.
concept.information_effect: Converts a retained physical association into a sequence-readable linkage between regions. It does not by itself establish exact distance, base pairing, direct contact, universal true-positive status or a quantitative interaction probability.
concept.purpose: Record relationships between nucleic-acid regions for later paired-region interpretation.
concept.context_requirements: Membership requires that joining two analyte regions is used to record their prior physical association. Merely attaching a known barcode to each analyte in a shared region is insufficient. DNA versus RNA, fixation/capture, direct versus linker-mediated joining, ligases, dilution, support, bridge sequence, controls and downstream biological interpretation remain contextual.
